_readme: Phase 1 of the sector-benchmarking upgrade proposed in the partner study 'دليل معايير المقارنة المعيارية حسب القطاع' (Sep 2026). Adds a free, zero-cost GLOBAL SECTOR AVERAGE reference, separate from and complementary to the manually-curated 23-company real-Tadawul-peer dataset in peer_benchmarks_seed.json. Do not merge the two: this file gives one INDUSTRY-WIDE AVERAGE per sector_code (no distribution, no named companies, no percentile — Damodaran publishes averages only, per the study's own Group C caveat), while peer_benchmarks_seed.json gives a real named-company cohort with quartiles. Scoped only to the three sector_code values Basira already uses (it_services, commercial_services, transport_logistics) — 'other' has no classification mapping and is intentionally left uncovered rather than guessed. Every code and figure below was fetched and read directly (UN ISIC Detail pages, NAICS/BLS/GICS sources via search, Damodaran's own published .xls files) on 2026-09-28; no figure is invented or estimated. If Damodaran's site or the classification sources change, this file goes stale silently until someone re-verifies — there is no live refresh.

global_average.source_name: Aswath Damodaran (NYU Stern) — Emerging Markets industry data
global_average.region: Emerging markets (Damodaran's regional grouping; includes Saudi Arabia/Gulf, not Saudi-specific)

metric_source_columns.ebit_margin: 'Pre-tax Unadjusted Operating Margin' column, margin dataset — matches Basira's own EBIT/revenue (pre-tax) definition, not an after-tax or lease-adjusted variant
metric_source_columns.receivables_days: Derived: 'Acc Rec/ Sales' column (working-capital dataset) × 365 — an approximation, not a true DSO, consistent with how Basira's own receivables_days is already an approximation (closing balance ÷ revenue × 365)

global_average.average_only_caveat: This is an industry AVERAGE across 693 firms, not a distribution — no median, quartiles or percentile can be derived from it. Do not present a company's position against this figure as a percentile rank; only as 'above/below the global sector average'.

parent_sector.title: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services

commercial_services.classification_caveat: Basira's commercial_services peer bucket mixes labor-outsourcing/staffing companies (Maharah, Al Mawarid, Tamkeen, SMASCO — 4 of 6 peers, matches this ISIC/NAICS/GICS code well) with a catering company (CATRION) and a facilities-management company (Shalfa), neither of which is an employment-services business. This classification is the best single fit for the majority of the bucket, not a perfect fit for all of it — the catering/facilities pair would properly sit under different ISIC/NAICS/GICS codes not mapped here.

global_average.source_name: Aswath Damodaran (NYU Stern) — Emerging Markets industry data
global_average.region: Emerging markets (Damodaran's regional grouping; includes Saudi Arabia/Gulf, not Saudi-specific)

metric_source_columns.ebit_margin: 'Pre-tax Unadjusted Operating Margin' column, margin dataset

global_average.industry_match_caveat: Damodaran does not publish a dedicated 'staffing/labor outsourcing' industry bucket. 'Business & Consumer Services' is his broadest general-services category and the closest available real match — it is not a labor-outsourcing-specific benchmark, so expect a wider gap to the actual peer companies than a purpose-built staffing index would show.
global_average.average_only_caveat: This is an industry AVERAGE across 379 firms, not a distribution — no median, quartiles or percentile can be derived from it.

isic.title: Transportation and storage
isic.note: Section-level, not a single division: this peer bucket spans land (division 49), water (division 50) and air (division 51) transport plus rental — no single ISIC division fits Bahri (marine), Flynas/SGS (air) and the car-rental companies (land) at once, so the honest mapping is the section that contains all of them.

naics.title: Transportation and Warehousing
naics.note: Sector-level for the same multi-modal reason as the ISIC mapping.

gics.title: Transportation
gics.note: Industry-group level. Sub-industries actually represented in this peer bucket span 'Passenger Airlines' (Flynas), 'Air Freight & Logistics' (SGS), 'Marine Transportation' (Bahri), and 'Cargo/Passenger Ground Transportation' (SAPTCO, car-rental companies) — again no single sub-industry code covers the whole bucket.

global_average.source_name: Aswath Damodaran (NYU Stern) — Emerging Markets industry data
global_average.region: Emerging markets (Damodaran's regional grouping; includes Saudi Arabia/Gulf, not Saudi-specific)

metric_source_columns.ebit_margin: 'Pre-tax Unadjusted Operating Margin' column, margin dataset

global_average.industry_match_caveat: Damodaran's single 'Transportation' category blends airlines, shipping, rail, trucking and rental together globally — the same multi-modal blending the peer bucket itself has, so this is a reasonably representative match, but it is still a broad average across very different transport economics (e.g. asset-light car rental vs. capital-intensive shipping), not a mode-specific benchmark.
global_average.average_only_caveat: This is an industry AVERAGE across 330 firms, not a distribution — no median, quartiles or percentile can be derived from it.
